findings.failure_mode: missing/unreadable file aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV field crashes the program instead of yielding a parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u16>()? or checked conversion, return Result, and map_err to a typed InvoiceParseError

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width-downcast from u32; silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a 32-bit value outside u16 range wraps to an incorrect Record without any error signal
findings.fix: replace with u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(...) or parse directly into u16 with checked conversion

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line and unbounded intermediate allocation on malformed lines
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').map(|(name, rest)| ...) to avoid Vec allocation and get exactly two halves

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] are unchecked indexed accesses on a user-controlled Vec
findings.failure_mode: a line with zero or one comma-separated fields panics with index out of bounds
findings.fix: use split_once and pattern-match (name, rest) or use .get() with Option/Result handling

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() clones a String from an unchecked Vec access
findings.failure_mode: redundant allocation + potential panic on short lines; also leaks data out of the split buffer
findings.fix: use the name string from split_once directly without cloning into an intermediate Vec

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a logging side effect inside a data-loading function
findings.failure_mode: impure core function that mutates global state (stdout), breaking determinism and testability
findings.fix: remove println!; push logging to the imperative shell at the call site

findings.problem: load_invoices returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures are unsignalled panics
findings.failure_mode: the caller has no way to distinguish I/O error, parse error, or format error; all manifest as panics
findings.fix: define a domain error enum (e.g. InvoiceError::Io / InvoiceError::Parse) and return Result<Vec<Record>, InvoiceError>

findings.problem: No try_reserve or allocation budget for the output Vec; capacity is unbounded
findings.failure_mode: large input files can cause OOM or excessive heap pressure without any bounded-allocation handling
findings.fix: use Vec::with_capacity(estimated) or pre-size from line count, and consider try_reserve with Allocation error handling if bounded

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_invoices
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify whether the split+collect+clone pattern is a performance problem or whether the function meets any throughput target
findings.fix: add a criterion or simple benchmark measuring bytes/ms and allocation count; use cargo-flamegraph or similar for profiler evidence

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists in the crate
findings.failure_mode: performance claims cannot be validated; no baseline for future optimizations
findings.fix: add a benchmarks/ directory or criterion integration with measured evidence for load_invoices throughput and memory
